findings.title: Transaction split PATCH is destructive but not marked idempotent or documented as replacing
findings.evidence: Description says line_items are 'create or replace' and an empty array 'unsplit (remove all line items)'; x-destructive: true, but no idempotency key parameter is defined on this operation.
findings.suggested_fix: Document replace semantics clearly, add an idempotency mechanism or If-Match/version check, and warn that omitting line_items leaves splits unchanged.

findings.title: Physical card POST response is documented as 200 with no error for create
findings.evidence: Success is 200 while sibling create endpoints return 201 (POST /cards/vault returns 201); the 400 error body is a bare string schema, unlike DeveloperApiErrorResponse used elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 201 for creation and use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 body to match the rest of the API.

findings.title: Success status codes inconsistent for GET single physical card
findings.evidence: Success response is documented as '201' for a read operation, while other GETs use 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200 for this read operation.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: summary: 'Permanently delete this resource' on a get operation; description is absent and it returns VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and ensure no delete semantics are implied.

findings.title: Card termination DELETE lacks correct documented behavior and irreversibility flags
findings.evidence: Description 'Please note that this action is irreversible.' is present but the operation has no 200/404 response documented and no x-destructive flag, unlike the transaction PATCH which has one.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 404 and state the terminal state outcome; mark destructive consistently.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter naming style
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter uses camelCase 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case 'user_id'; transactions sort uses 'orderByAmountAsc' alongside 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to snake_case (user_id, order_by_amount_asc) and keep the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Inconsistent pagination and page-size semantics across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Physical cards list has no start/page_size parameters at all; virtual, reimbursements and transactions use 'start' and page_size with range 2-100, and only transactions offers include_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Give every list endpoint the same pagination parameters and document the page_size bounds and cursor behavior uniformly.

findings.title: Transaction 'amount' field documented as number on one schema and string on another
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type 'number' while SingleTransaction.amount is type 'string', both marked deprecated.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the deprecated amount type identical across the list and single-fetch schemas.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'sync_status' and 'trace_id' read-only fields lack consistent nullability
findings.evidence: Transaction.sync_status and SingleTransaction.sync_status have no 'nullable' or 'enum' differences, yet Transaction.sync_status is absent from the 'required' list in SingleTransaction despite being in its required array; sync_status in Transaction has no type-level 'enum' in SingleTransaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Make sync_status definitions identical with explicit enums across Transaction, SingleTransaction, and Reimbursement.

findings.title: Vault card creation endpoint combines unrelated actions and returns sensitive PAN/CVV
findings.evidence: Summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' combines limit creation and PAN/CVV disclosure; response PCILimit includes card.pan and card.cvv, and the X-Idempotency-Key header is optional.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the idempotency key required for this write that creates a limit and returns card secrets, and split the summary into accurate separate concerns.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload uses different idempotency mechanism than vault creation
findings.evidence: Receipt upload takes idempotency_key as a required multipart body field, while the vault creation uses optional X-Idempotency-Key header; the path also uses singular 'reimbursement' while other paths use 'reimbursements'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header, required) across writes and align the path to '/reimbursements/submit-receipt'.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security and no error responses
findings.evidence: 'security': [] overrides the global scheme so no OAuth scope is required, though the operation creates financial reimbursements; only a 401 is documented, and the operation body has no 400.
findings.suggested_fix: Require oauth2 reimbursements:write on this operation and document 400 and 403 responses.

findings.title: Physical card PATCH and POST omit documented 400/404 responses and reference bare string errors
findings.evidence: PATCH lists only 200; the POST 400 body is typed as plain string while other 400s reference DeveloperApiErrorResponse, so clients cannot parse error_code reliably.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the full error set and use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for every error response.

findings.title: Duplicate 'Transaction' tag and unexplained 'transactions' tag
findings.evidence: Tags include 'Transaction' and a separate 'transactions' tag with no description, and the PATCH operation is tagged with both.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge into a single documented 'Transaction' tag.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH marked destructive and documented as replacing splits
findings.evidence: Description says line_items 'create or replace the transaction's split' and an empty array 'unsplit (remove all line items)'; the operation is tagged x-destructive: true and x-read-only: false, but no idempotency key is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that retries are safe (or accept X-Idempotency-Key) and state clearly that the call overwrites existing line items and their memos/coding.

findings.title: Pagination inconsistent: 'start' cursor semantics and page_size bounds
findings.evidence: Virtual cards page_size is documented as 'between 2 and 100' with default 20 but the schema has no min/max; start is described as 'the ID of the last entity of the previous page' yet is an untyped string, and physical cards list has no pagination params at all despite returning PaginatedResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one pagination scheme across list endpoints, with minimum/maximum set in the schema and a documented cursor format; add paging params to the physical cards list or document its limits.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'user' parameter naming across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is camelCase 'userId' while every other filter is snake_case, e.g. 'entity_id' and 'user_id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename 'userId' to 'user_id' and keep the old name as a deprecated alias for compatibility.

findings.title: Naming conflict between 'fund_id' and 'limit_id' / 'spend_limit_id'
findings.location: Transaction, Reimbursement, PCILimit schemas; GET /developer/v1/transactions (limit_id filter)
findings.evidence: Transactions expose fund_id, limit_id (deprecated alias) and the reimbursement has spend_limit_id (deprecated); the transaction list filter is limit_id while the response says fund_id 'Returns the same value as limit_id'; the card vault/request still use spend_limit terminology.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on fund_id across filters, request bodies and responses, and mark every legacy alias deprecated in the same way.

findings.title: Mismatched success status codes for the same resource
findings.evidence: GET physical card returns 201 instead of 200; the vault POST returns 201 but is described as 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details'.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for reads and document the correct success code for each operation.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented or typed as bare string
findings.evidence: POST physical cards 400 uses schema type 'string' rather than DeveloperApiErrorResponse; PATCH physical card and POST mileage lack 400 responses entirely; mileage has security [] but declares 401.
findings.suggested_fix: Use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all error responses and document every error code each operation can return.

findings.title: Security requirements inconsistent across operations
findings.evidence: Operation sets "security": [] which overrides the global/no-scope default and returns 401 Unauthorized, implying authentication is optional or undefined.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the oauth2 requirement with the correct scope (reimbursements:write) for this operation.

findings.title: Sensitive PAN/CVV returned with weak scope and no warnings
findings.evidence: CardDetails returns pan and cvv; PCICardDetails and CardShipping.full_card_number also expose full card numbers, but no description warns about handling, and the vault response is labeled by the scope cards:read_vault only.
findings.suggested_fix: Document PCI handling requirements, restrict the response to necessary fields, and add explicit descriptions noting sensitivity on each field.

findings.title: Reimbursement list state filter lists values not in documented enum meaning
findings.evidence: Parameter 'direction' default BUSINESS_TO_USER and state x-enum-descriptions include 'PUSH_PAYMENT_INITIATED':'Scheduled' and 'REIMBURSED_VIA_PUSH':'Paid' with ambiguous, overlapping labels for the same states.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each state a precise, non-overlapping description and document the state transitions.

findings.title: Boolean default and filter semantics ambiguous for physical cards
findings.evidence: include_activated_only 'Defaults to True if not specified' and include_terminated_only 'Defaults to False', yet the description says filters are by 'activation status, termination status' and the schema has no default values.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the defaults in the schema and clarify whether terminated and unactivated cards are included by default.

findings.title: Deprecated 'amount' field still typed differently across schemas
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type number while SingleTransaction.amount is type string, both marked deprecated, for the same concept.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for the same field across schemas and remove the deprecated field in a future version.

findings.title: Wrong or mismatched operation summaries
findings.evidence: GET virtual card is summarized 'Permanently delete this resource', which is wrong and dangerous; the DELETE suspension is 'Unsuspend a card' but the POST suspension says 'Suspend a card' with no description linking them.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and cross-reference suspend/unsuspend operations.

findings.title: Duplicate tag 'transactions' conflicts with 'Transaction'
findings.evidence: The top-level tags list has 'Transaction' and a separate 'transactions' tag, and the PATCH operation uses both tags.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single tag 'Transaction' and remove the duplicate.

findings.title: Typo and incomplete operation description
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date has description 'Data.' and the transactions include_merchant_data and transaction_id include_merchant_data param is also 'Data.'; CardDetails.expiration is marked readOnly yet required in a create response.
findings.suggested_fix: Write meaningful descriptions for each parameter and reconcile readOnly fields with required lists.

findings.title: POST /cards/physical documents a 200 response for creation
findings.evidence: Responses only define '200' with description 'Success' for creating a physical card, while sibling create endpoints (e.g. POST /cards/vault) return 201.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 201 Created for resource creation and document it, or document the actual status code.

findings.title: GET /cards/physical/{card_id} documents 201 instead of 200
findings.evidence: The only success response is '201' with description 'Success' for a read operation.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the success response as 200 for GET.

findings.title: Virtual card DELETE-style summary on a GET operation
findings.evidence: Summary reads 'Permanently delete this resource' on a GET operation that returns a VirtualCard; no DELETE operation exists on this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Change summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' so it matches the operation's behavior.

findings.title: Duplicate/conflicting tags and undefined tag group
findings.evidence: Tags 'Transaction' and 'transactions' both exist, and the PATCH split operation uses both, so docs group the same resource under two names.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 'transactions' tag and use a single 'Transaction' tag consistently.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH is destructive with ambiguous replace semantics
findings.evidence: Description says line_items 'create or replace' the split and that an empty array 'unsplit (remove all line items)', flagged x-destructive: true, yet no idempotency key or confirmation mechanism is defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the replace semantics explicitly and support X-Idempotency-Key or a dry-run for destructive updates.

findings.title: Pagination parameters inconsistent between list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use 'start' and 'page_size' (default 20) but the virtual card list has no include_count option, while transactions use include_count; the 'start' parameter is documented as 'ID of the last entity' yet is typed as a free string with no format.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize pagination parameters and response page fields across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Inconsistent naming of query parameters
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter uses camelCase 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case 'user_id'; transactions mixes 'orderByAmountAsc' with 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use snake_case consistently, e.g. user_id and order_by_amount_asc, and deprecate the camelCase forms.

findings.title: Misleading sk_category_id type in response schema
findings.evidence: Schema declares type integer with enum, but the example returns the string "40,41" with sk_category_name 'SaaS / Software', which is not in the enum.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the example and make the schema reflect whether multiple category codes can be returned.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload has undocumented idempotency header vs body field
findings.evidence: Requires 'idempotency_key' in the multipart body, while POST /cards/vault uses an X-Idempotency-Key header; the two mechanisms differ and the create-card endpoint documents the key as optional.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header) across all create endpoints and make it consistently required or clearly documented as optional.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt endpoint path diverges from resource path
findings.evidence: Uses singular 'reimbursement' while all other reimbursement paths use plural '/developer/v1/reimbursements'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/receipts or similar plural resource path.

findings.title: Vault creation returns PCI card data with mismatched response type
findings.evidence: Summary says 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' but the response is PCILimit, and the request requires user_id while the response documents card and restrictions as readOnly inside the same object.
findings.suggested_fix: Split spend-limit creation from sensitive-data retrieval, or clearly document the combined response contract.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented for many operations and mixed error shapes
findings.evidence: The 400 response is a plain 'type: string' rather than DeveloperApiErrorResponse used elsewhere, and PATCH/GET operations on physical cards and transactions list no 4xx/401 responses at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the standard DeveloperApiErrorResponse schema for all error responses and document 401/403/404 on every operation.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement declares no security yet lists 401
findings.evidence: Operation sets 'security: []' (no auth required) yet documents a 401 Unauthorized response.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the empty security override so the operation requires reimbursements:write, or drop the 401 contradiction.

findings.title: Card detail endpoints lack documented scope guidance on sensitive data
findings.evidence: Returns pan and cvv with no description of sensitivity, logging restrictions, or caching rules, and 'pan' is not marked as sensitive or writeOnly.
findings.suggested_fix: Document sensitivity, caching restrictions, and required PCI handling in the operation description.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH is destructive but not flagged in docs
findings.evidence: Operation is marked x-destructive: true, yet the description only says line_items replace the split; sending an empty array silently removes all line items.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a prominent warning in the description and a 409/400 response for invalid sums, and document that replacement discards existing line-item memos and selections.

findings.title: Splitting a transaction tagged as 'transactions' duplicate tag
findings.evidence: tags: ["Transaction","transactions"] — two tags differing only by case, and the separate top-level tag 'transactions' is declared without a matching group.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the single 'Transaction' tag and remove the lowercase 'transactions' tag.

findings.title: Create physical card POST error response is untyped string
findings.evidence: 400 response content schema is type: string, while every other 400 uses DeveloperApiErrorResponse with error_v2 and error_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Return DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 response, matching the rest of the API.

findings.title: Inconsistent 2xx codes for the single-resource GET
findings.evidence: Success is documented as 201 Created for a read operation, while the sibling GET endpoints return 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200 for the GET operation.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete'
findings.evidence: summary: "Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation that fetches a single virtual card and returns 200 VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and verify no delete operation was intended.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security but 401 response
findings.evidence: security: [] overrides the global-level expectation, yet the operation documents a 401 Unauthorized response and no scope is listed.
findings.suggested_fix: Set security to the reimbursements:write oauth2 scope like other reimbursement write operations, or document why it is unauthenticated.

findings.title: Receipt upload documents idempotency twice with different names
findings.evidence: Body field idempotency_key is required, but the endpoint does not take the X-Idempotency-Key header used by POST /cards/vault; the two idempotency mechanisms are inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header X-Idempotency-Key) across all create endpoints and document its retention window.

findings.title: Path inconsistency: 'reimbursement' vs 'reimbursements'
findings.evidence: All other reimbursement paths use /developer/v1/reimbursements, but this one uses singular /reimbursement/submit-receipt.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/receipts or similar plural form and keep the old path as a deprecated alias.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter naming styles
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use userId (camelCase) while everywhere else uses user_id; transactions use orderByAmountAsc alongside order_by_amount_desc.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId and orderByAmountAsc to snake_case and keep the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Pagination inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Physical cards list has no start or page_size parameters, but returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a next link; virtual cards and reimbursements accept start and page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters to the physical card list, matching the other list endpoints.

findings.title: Deprecated amount fields still returned without guidance
findings.location: Transaction schema properties amount and currency_code
findings.evidence: amount is typed number in Transaction but type string in SingleTransaction, and both are marked deprecated; the two schemas disagree on the type of the same field.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the type consistent across Transaction and SingleTransaction and document the sunset date for amount and currency_code.

findings.title: Filter boolean defaults contradicted by description
findings.evidence: include_activated_only says it 'Defaults to True' but the schema has no default, and the description says 'Filter only for activated cards', which conflicts with listing unactivated cards by default.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare default: true in the schema and state the effective default clearly.

findings.title: Reimbursement sync filter parameters overlap
findings.evidence: sync_status 'Supersedes has_no_sync_commits and sync_ready', yet all three are still accepted and no precedence is stated for the transaction endpoint's equivalent parameters beyond a single sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits as deprecated in the schema and document the precedence rules.

findings.title: Vague parameter description 'Data.'
findings.evidence: include_merchant_data and to_transaction_date are described only as 'Data.', giving no meaning to the developer.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a real description of the filter's behaviour and the expected format.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH marked destructive but described as split update
findings.evidence: Description says line_items replace the existing split and an empty array removes all line items; the operation is tagged x-destructive: true yet the response is a 200 with no documented idempotency or confirmation mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Document clearly that the PATCH replaces existing line items and that unsplitting is irreversible, and document any safeguards.

findings.title: Physical card DELETE is named 'Terminate' but no 204 error on not found
findings.evidence: Only 204 and 400 are documented; no 404 is listed even though the card_id path parameter can reference a nonexistent card, while sibling GET/PATCH also omit 404.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 404 (and 401/403) responses consistently across all single-resource operations.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: The summary field for the GET operation reads 'Permanently delete this resource' while the operation fetches a single virtual card and no DELETE exists for this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and remove the misleading deletion wording.

findings.title: Card creation endpoint has contradictory 201 vs 200 responses and wrong schema
findings.evidence: GET single physical card returns 201 instead of 200, POST creates physical card returns 200 with a PhysicalCard schema, and POST /cards/vault returns 201 with PCILimit schema; success codes are inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 200 for reads and 201 for creations consistently, and correct the GET /cards/physical/{card_id} success code to 200.

findings.title: Vault create operation returns limit schema, mislabelled as card creation
findings.evidence: Summary is 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' and the response is PCILimit, while the operationId is post_card_vault_creation and the path is cards/vault, so the resource returned is a limit not a card.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the operation and path to reflect the spend limit creation, or split card-detail retrieval from limit creation.

findings.title: Security-sensitive vault endpoints without documented PCI handling
findings.evidence: CardDetails returns full PAN and CVV in a 200 response, with no description of caching headers, rate limits, or restrictions; the only protection is an OAuth scope cards:read_vault.
findings.suggested_fix: Document no-store caching requirements, audit logging, and the sensitivity of the response in the operation description.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security yet 401 response
findings.evidence: The operation sets security: [] (no auth) yet documents a 401 Unauthorized response, which is contradictory for a create operation that mutates financial data.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the oauth2 reimbursements:write scope to this operation and remove the empty security override.

findings.title: Pagination inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards list uses start and page_size, with no page_size bounds in the physical cards list, and physical cards has no pagination parameters at all while returning a paginated response schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters with consistent bounds to the physical cards list and use the same pattern across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter naming style
findings.evidence: Parameter userId is camelCase while all others are snake_case like user_id; orderByAmountAsc is camelCase while order_by_amount_desc is snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId to user_id and orderByAmountAsc to order_by_amount_asc, keeping the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Ambiguous and overlapping sync filter parameters on reimbursements
findings.evidence: sync_status says it supersedes has_no_sync_commits and sync_ready, but all three remain as independent filters with no precedence stated for combinations or deprecation notice.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits as deprecated and document the precedence explicitly.

findings.title: Transaction state default is undocumented for list endpoint
findings.evidence: Description says if state is not set all transactions except declined are returned, but the state enum has no default and 'ALL' is described as special, making the default behaviour easy to misread.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the default explicitly in the schema and clarify how 'ALL' differs from the unset default.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload uses undocumented idempotency mechanisms
findings.evidence: Body has an idempotency_key field and the vault endpoint has an X-Idempotency-Key header, but the receipt upload does not use the header and the vault create operation marks the header optional, so retries have no uniform contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism across write endpoints and make it required or clearly documented as to behaviour on duplicates.

findings.title: Path naming inconsistent between reimbursement endpoints
findings.evidence: The receipt endpoint uses singular 'reimbursement' while all other reimbursement paths use plural 'reimbursements'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the path to /developer/v1/reimbursements/submit-receipt or similar plural form.

findings.title: Deprecated amount fields still returned with type conflicts
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type number while SingleTransaction.amount is type string for the same deprecated field, so the same resource returns different types depending on endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the amount type consistent across Transaction and SingleTransaction schemas.

findings.title: Card holder and reimbursement ID fields missing relationship to parent operations
findings.evidence: PhysicalCard.required includes display_name, expiration, fulfillment and last_four, which are readOnly, while id and state are not required, making the required list inconsistent with the documented response shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the required array with fields that the server always returns, and remove readOnly fields from the required list where appropriate.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH is a destructive split but not marked idempotent or documented
findings.evidence: Operation is marked "x-destructive":true and replaces existing splits, but has no idempotency guidance and no X-Idempotency-Key header, unlike POST /developer/v1/cards/vault.
findings.suggested_fix: Document replace semantics explicitly and offer an idempotency key or a conditional/version check for retries.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload defines idempotency_key in body, not header
findings.evidence: idempotency_key is a required multipart field, while POST /developer/v1/cards/vault uses an X-Idempotency-Key header (optional), and no other POST documents idempotency at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header X-Idempotency-Key) across all mutating endpoints and state whether it is required.

findings.title: Card vault POST has an optional idempotency key despite creating funds limits and cards
findings.evidence: The header is "required": false, yet the operation creates a card and a spend limit; a retry without the key may create duplicates.
findings.suggested_fix: Make X-Idempotency-Key required for this create operation or document the duplicate behavior when omitted.

findings.title: Physical card POST and vault endpoints lack documented 4xx/409 errors
findings.evidence: The 400 response is typed as a plain string schema, while every other error uses DeveloperApiErrorResponse; no 401/403/404/409 is declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Return DeveloperApiErrorResponse for 400 and declare 401, 403, 404, and 409 where applicable.

findings.title: Success status codes inconsistent for GET physical card
findings.evidence: Success is documented as 201 Created for a read operation, while the list and other GETs use 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: summary: "Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation that fetches a single virtual card; there is no DELETE on this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card'.

findings.title: Physical card DELETE described as termination; suspension verbs swapped
findings.evidence: POST is 'Suspend a card' and DELETE is 'Unsuspend a card' (correct), but the POST description says 'The suspension is revertable' with no link to the unsuspend operation; DELETE /cards/physical/{card_id} is 'Terminate a card' with the warning only in description, which conflicts with DELETE semantics for a reversible-looking resource.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the terminate operation with a non-DELETE-implying summary or document that DELETE is irreversible in the summary itself and link the suspension operations.

findings.title: Transactions 'state' filter default behavior is ambiguous
findings.evidence: Description says non-declined transactions are returned when state is unset, and the enum lacks a default, while 'ALL' is documented as including DECLINED.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit default to the schema and an example showing the default filtering.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter casing and sort parameter styles
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case user_id; transactions mix orderByAmountAsc with order_by_amount_desc and order_by_date_asc.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to snake_case (user_id, order_by_amount_asc) and deprecate the old names.

findings.title: Pagination param 'start' is inconsistent with cursor semantics and sort in lists
findings.evidence: 'start' is described as 'the ID of the last entity of the previous page', but physical cards list has no pagination params at all and page_size has no documented maximum in schema, only in description.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an opaque cursor named consistently (e.g. cursor) across list endpoints and add maximum/minimum to the page_size schema.

findings.title: Physical card list has pagination response but no pagination parameters
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a page.next link, yet the parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only; no start or page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters matching the other list endpoints.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no auth yet is a write
findings.evidence: "security": [] overrides global access and no scope is required, yet the endpoint creates a reimbursement; only a 401 is documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Require oauth2 with reimbursements:write scope and remove the empty security override.

findings.title: Card vault create response and tag/scope misuse for sensitive data
findings.evidence: Operation returns PCILimit containing full card PAN and CVV, and the summary says 'Create a spend limit' while the scope is 'cards:read_vault' plus 'limits:write'; the create operation is not marked with any sensitive-data flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Split spend-limit creation from sensitive detail retrieval and mark sensitive responses with a clear warning and cache-control guidance.

findings.title: Physical card fetch returns full card number in shipping
findings.evidence: CardShipping includes a 'full_card_number' string property, yet PhysicalCard returns fulfillment.shipping on GET and list endpoints marked x-uses-read-replica, with no sensitivity or scope note.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove full_card_number from non-vault responses or document it as sensitive with a distinct read_vault scope.

findings.title: Transaction 'amount' documented as deprecated but typed inconsistently
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type number while SingleTransaction.amount is type string, both marked deprecated 'Use entity_amount'; entity_amount itself uses minor-unit integers.
findings.suggested_fix: Make both schemas identical in type and state the deprecation removal date.

findings.title: Transaction split PATCH is destructive but not marked idempotent or documented as replacing
findings.evidence: Description says line_items are 'create or replace' and an empty array 'unsplit (remove all line items)'; x-destructive: true, but no idempotency key parameter is defined on this operation.
findings.suggested_fix: Document replace semantics clearly, add an idempotency mechanism or If-Match/version check, and warn that omitting line_items leaves splits unchanged.

findings.title: Physical card POST response is documented as 200 with no error for create
findings.evidence: Success is 200 while sibling create endpoints return 201 (POST /cards/vault returns 201); the 400 error body is a bare string schema, unlike DeveloperApiErrorResponse used elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 201 for creation and use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 body to match the rest of the API.

findings.title: Success status codes inconsistent for GET single physical card
findings.evidence: Success response is documented as '201' for a read operation, while other GETs use 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200 for this read operation.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: summary: 'Permanently delete this resource' on a get operation; description is absent and it returns VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and ensure no delete semantics are implied.

findings.title: Card termination DELETE lacks correct documented behavior and irreversibility flags
findings.evidence: Description 'Please note that this action is irreversible.' is present but the operation has no 200/404 response documented and no x-destructive flag, unlike the transaction PATCH which has one.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 404 and state the terminal state outcome; mark destructive consistently.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter naming style
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter uses camelCase 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case 'user_id'; transactions sort uses 'orderByAmountAsc' alongside 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to snake_case (user_id, order_by_amount_asc) and keep the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Inconsistent pagination and page-size semantics across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Physical cards list has no start/page_size parameters at all; virtual, reimbursements and transactions use 'start' and page_size with range 2-100, and only transactions offers include_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Give every list endpoint the same pagination parameters and document the page_size bounds and cursor behavior uniformly.

findings.title: Transaction 'amount' field documented as number on one schema and string on another
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type 'number' while SingleTransaction.amount is type 'string', both marked deprecated.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the deprecated amount type identical across the list and single-fetch schemas.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'sync_status' and 'trace_id' read-only fields lack consistent nullability
findings.evidence: Transaction.sync_status and SingleTransaction.sync_status have no 'nullable' or 'enum' differences, yet Transaction.sync_status is absent from the 'required' list in SingleTransaction despite being in its required array; sync_status in Transaction has no type-level 'enum' in SingleTransaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Make sync_status definitions identical with explicit enums across Transaction, SingleTransaction, and Reimbursement.

findings.title: Vault card creation endpoint combines unrelated actions and returns sensitive PAN/CVV
findings.evidence: Summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' combines limit creation and PAN/CVV disclosure; response PCILimit includes card.pan and card.cvv, and the X-Idempotency-Key header is optional.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the idempotency key required for this write that creates a limit and returns card secrets, and split the summary into accurate separate concerns.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload uses different idempotency mechanism than vault creation
findings.evidence: Receipt upload takes idempotency_key as a required multipart body field, while the vault creation uses optional X-Idempotency-Key header; the path also uses singular 'reimbursement' while other paths use 'reimbursements'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header, required) across writes and align the path to '/reimbursements/submit-receipt'.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security and no error responses
findings.evidence: 'security': [] overrides the global scheme so no OAuth scope is required, though the operation creates financial reimbursements; only a 401 is documented, and the operation body has no 400.
findings.suggested_fix: Require oauth2 reimbursements:write on this operation and document 400 and 403 responses.

findings.title: Physical card PATCH and POST omit documented 400/404 responses and reference bare string errors
findings.evidence: PATCH lists only 200; the POST 400 body is typed as plain string while other 400s reference DeveloperApiErrorResponse, so clients cannot parse error_code reliably.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the full error set and use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for every error response.

findings.title: Duplicate 'Transaction' tag and unexplained 'transactions' tag
findings.evidence: Tags include 'Transaction' and a separate 'transactions' tag with no description, and the PATCH operation is tagged with both.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge into a single documented 'Transaction' tag.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH marked destructive and documented as replacing splits
findings.evidence: Description says line_items 'create or replace the transaction's split' and an empty array 'unsplit (remove all line items)'; the operation is tagged x-destructive: true and x-read-only: false, but no idempotency key is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that retries are safe (or accept X-Idempotency-Key) and state clearly that the call overwrites existing line items and their memos/coding.

findings.title: Pagination inconsistent: 'start' cursor semantics and page_size bounds
findings.evidence: Virtual cards page_size is documented as 'between 2 and 100' with default 20 but the schema has no min/max; start is described as 'the ID of the last entity of the previous page' yet is an untyped string, and physical cards list has no pagination params at all despite returning PaginatedResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one pagination scheme across list endpoints, with minimum/maximum set in the schema and a documented cursor format; add paging params to the physical cards list or document its limits.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'user' parameter naming across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is camelCase 'userId' while every other filter is snake_case, e.g. 'entity_id' and 'user_id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename 'userId' to 'user_id' and keep the old name as a deprecated alias for compatibility.

findings.title: Naming conflict between 'fund_id' and 'limit_id' / 'spend_limit_id'
findings.location: Transaction, Reimbursement, PCILimit schemas; GET /developer/v1/transactions (limit_id filter)
findings.evidence: Transactions expose fund_id, limit_id (deprecated alias) and the reimbursement has spend_limit_id (deprecated); the transaction list filter is limit_id while the response says fund_id 'Returns the same value as limit_id'; the card vault/request still use spend_limit terminology.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on fund_id across filters, request bodies and responses, and mark every legacy alias deprecated in the same way.

findings.title: Mismatched success status codes for the same resource
findings.evidence: GET physical card returns 201 instead of 200; the vault POST returns 201 but is described as 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details'.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for reads and document the correct success code for each operation.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented or typed as bare string
findings.evidence: POST physical cards 400 uses schema type 'string' rather than DeveloperApiErrorResponse; PATCH physical card and POST mileage lack 400 responses entirely; mileage has security [] but declares 401.
findings.suggested_fix: Use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all error responses and document every error code each operation can return.

findings.title: Security requirements inconsistent across operations
findings.evidence: Operation sets "security": [] which overrides the global/no-scope default and returns 401 Unauthorized, implying authentication is optional or undefined.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the oauth2 requirement with the correct scope (reimbursements:write) for this operation.

findings.title: Sensitive PAN/CVV returned with weak scope and no warnings
findings.evidence: CardDetails returns pan and cvv; PCICardDetails and CardShipping.full_card_number also expose full card numbers, but no description warns about handling, and the vault response is labeled by the scope cards:read_vault only.
findings.suggested_fix: Document PCI handling requirements, restrict the response to necessary fields, and add explicit descriptions noting sensitivity on each field.

findings.title: Reimbursement list state filter lists values not in documented enum meaning
findings.evidence: Parameter 'direction' default BUSINESS_TO_USER and state x-enum-descriptions include 'PUSH_PAYMENT_INITIATED':'Scheduled' and 'REIMBURSED_VIA_PUSH':'Paid' with ambiguous, overlapping labels for the same states.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each state a precise, non-overlapping description and document the state transitions.

findings.title: Boolean default and filter semantics ambiguous for physical cards
findings.evidence: include_activated_only 'Defaults to True if not specified' and include_terminated_only 'Defaults to False', yet the description says filters are by 'activation status, termination status' and the schema has no default values.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the defaults in the schema and clarify whether terminated and unactivated cards are included by default.

findings.title: Deprecated 'amount' field still typed differently across schemas
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type number while SingleTransaction.amount is type string, both marked deprecated, for the same concept.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for the same field across schemas and remove the deprecated field in a future version.

findings.title: Wrong or mismatched operation summaries
findings.evidence: GET virtual card is summarized 'Permanently delete this resource', which is wrong and dangerous; the DELETE suspension is 'Unsuspend a card' but the POST suspension says 'Suspend a card' with no description linking them.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and cross-reference suspend/unsuspend operations.

findings.title: Duplicate tag 'transactions' conflicts with 'Transaction'
findings.evidence: The top-level tags list has 'Transaction' and a separate 'transactions' tag, and the PATCH operation uses both tags.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single tag 'Transaction' and remove the duplicate.

findings.title: Typo and incomplete operation description
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date has description 'Data.' and the transactions include_merchant_data and transaction_id include_merchant_data param is also 'Data.'; CardDetails.expiration is marked readOnly yet required in a create response.
findings.suggested_fix: Write meaningful descriptions for each parameter and reconcile readOnly fields with required lists.

findings.title: POST /cards/physical documents a 200 response for creation
findings.evidence: Responses only define '200' with description 'Success' for creating a physical card, while sibling create endpoints (e.g. POST /cards/vault) return 201.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 201 Created for resource creation and document it, or document the actual status code.

findings.title: GET /cards/physical/{card_id} documents 201 instead of 200
findings.evidence: The only success response is '201' with description 'Success' for a read operation.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the success response as 200 for GET.

findings.title: Virtual card DELETE-style summary on a GET operation
findings.evidence: Summary reads 'Permanently delete this resource' on a GET operation that returns a VirtualCard; no DELETE operation exists on this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Change summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' so it matches the operation's behavior.

findings.title: Duplicate/conflicting tags and undefined tag group
findings.evidence: Tags 'Transaction' and 'transactions' both exist, and the PATCH split operation uses both, so docs group the same resource under two names.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 'transactions' tag and use a single 'Transaction' tag consistently.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH is destructive with ambiguous replace semantics
findings.evidence: Description says line_items 'create or replace' the split and that an empty array 'unsplit (remove all line items)', flagged x-destructive: true, yet no idempotency key or confirmation mechanism is defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the replace semantics explicitly and support X-Idempotency-Key or a dry-run for destructive updates.

findings.title: Pagination parameters inconsistent between list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use 'start' and 'page_size' (default 20) but the virtual card list has no include_count option, while transactions use include_count; the 'start' parameter is documented as 'ID of the last entity' yet is typed as a free string with no format.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize pagination parameters and response page fields across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Inconsistent naming of query parameters
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter uses camelCase 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case 'user_id'; transactions mixes 'orderByAmountAsc' with 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use snake_case consistently, e.g. user_id and order_by_amount_asc, and deprecate the camelCase forms.

findings.title: Misleading sk_category_id type in response schema
findings.evidence: Schema declares type integer with enum, but the example returns the string "40,41" with sk_category_name 'SaaS / Software', which is not in the enum.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the example and make the schema reflect whether multiple category codes can be returned.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload has undocumented idempotency header vs body field
findings.evidence: Requires 'idempotency_key' in the multipart body, while POST /cards/vault uses an X-Idempotency-Key header; the two mechanisms differ and the create-card endpoint documents the key as optional.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header) across all create endpoints and make it consistently required or clearly documented as optional.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt endpoint path diverges from resource path
findings.evidence: Uses singular 'reimbursement' while all other reimbursement paths use plural '/developer/v1/reimbursements'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/receipts or similar plural resource path.

findings.title: Vault creation returns PCI card data with mismatched response type
findings.evidence: Summary says 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' but the response is PCILimit, and the request requires user_id while the response documents card and restrictions as readOnly inside the same object.
findings.suggested_fix: Split spend-limit creation from sensitive-data retrieval, or clearly document the combined response contract.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented for many operations and mixed error shapes
findings.evidence: The 400 response is a plain 'type: string' rather than DeveloperApiErrorResponse used elsewhere, and PATCH/GET operations on physical cards and transactions list no 4xx/401 responses at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the standard DeveloperApiErrorResponse schema for all error responses and document 401/403/404 on every operation.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement declares no security yet lists 401
findings.evidence: Operation sets 'security: []' (no auth required) yet documents a 401 Unauthorized response.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the empty security override so the operation requires reimbursements:write, or drop the 401 contradiction.

findings.title: Card detail endpoints lack documented scope guidance on sensitive data
findings.evidence: Returns pan and cvv with no description of sensitivity, logging restrictions, or caching rules, and 'pan' is not marked as sensitive or writeOnly.
findings.suggested_fix: Document sensitivity, caching restrictions, and required PCI handling in the operation description.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH is destructive but not flagged in docs
findings.evidence: Operation is marked x-destructive: true, yet the description only says line_items replace the split; sending an empty array silently removes all line items.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a prominent warning in the description and a 409/400 response for invalid sums, and document that replacement discards existing line-item memos and selections.

findings.title: Splitting a transaction tagged as 'transactions' duplicate tag
findings.evidence: tags: ["Transaction","transactions"] — two tags differing only by case, and the separate top-level tag 'transactions' is declared without a matching group.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the single 'Transaction' tag and remove the lowercase 'transactions' tag.

findings.title: Create physical card POST error response is untyped string
findings.evidence: 400 response content schema is type: string, while every other 400 uses DeveloperApiErrorResponse with error_v2 and error_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Return DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 response, matching the rest of the API.

findings.title: Inconsistent 2xx codes for the single-resource GET
findings.evidence: Success is documented as 201 Created for a read operation, while the sibling GET endpoints return 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200 for the GET operation.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete'
findings.evidence: summary: "Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation that fetches a single virtual card and returns 200 VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and verify no delete operation was intended.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security but 401 response
findings.evidence: security: [] overrides the global-level expectation, yet the operation documents a 401 Unauthorized response and no scope is listed.
findings.suggested_fix: Set security to the reimbursements:write oauth2 scope like other reimbursement write operations, or document why it is unauthenticated.

findings.title: Receipt upload documents idempotency twice with different names
findings.evidence: Body field idempotency_key is required, but the endpoint does not take the X-Idempotency-Key header used by POST /cards/vault; the two idempotency mechanisms are inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header X-Idempotency-Key) across all create endpoints and document its retention window.

findings.title: Path inconsistency: 'reimbursement' vs 'reimbursements'
findings.evidence: All other reimbursement paths use /developer/v1/reimbursements, but this one uses singular /reimbursement/submit-receipt.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/receipts or similar plural form and keep the old path as a deprecated alias.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter naming styles
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use userId (camelCase) while everywhere else uses user_id; transactions use orderByAmountAsc alongside order_by_amount_desc.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId and orderByAmountAsc to snake_case and keep the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Pagination inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Physical cards list has no start or page_size parameters, but returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a next link; virtual cards and reimbursements accept start and page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters to the physical card list, matching the other list endpoints.

findings.title: Deprecated amount fields still returned without guidance
findings.location: Transaction schema properties amount and currency_code
findings.evidence: amount is typed number in Transaction but type string in SingleTransaction, and both are marked deprecated; the two schemas disagree on the type of the same field.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the type consistent across Transaction and SingleTransaction and document the sunset date for amount and currency_code.

findings.title: Filter boolean defaults contradicted by description
findings.evidence: include_activated_only says it 'Defaults to True' but the schema has no default, and the description says 'Filter only for activated cards', which conflicts with listing unactivated cards by default.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare default: true in the schema and state the effective default clearly.

findings.title: Reimbursement sync filter parameters overlap
findings.evidence: sync_status 'Supersedes has_no_sync_commits and sync_ready', yet all three are still accepted and no precedence is stated for the transaction endpoint's equivalent parameters beyond a single sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits as deprecated in the schema and document the precedence rules.

findings.title: Vague parameter description 'Data.'
findings.evidence: include_merchant_data and to_transaction_date are described only as 'Data.', giving no meaning to the developer.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a real description of the filter's behaviour and the expected format.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH marked destructive but described as split update
findings.evidence: Description says line_items replace the existing split and an empty array removes all line items; the operation is tagged x-destructive: true yet the response is a 200 with no documented idempotency or confirmation mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Document clearly that the PATCH replaces existing line items and that unsplitting is irreversible, and document any safeguards.

findings.title: Physical card DELETE is named 'Terminate' but no 204 error on not found
findings.evidence: Only 204 and 400 are documented; no 404 is listed even though the card_id path parameter can reference a nonexistent card, while sibling GET/PATCH also omit 404.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 404 (and 401/403) responses consistently across all single-resource operations.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: The summary field for the GET operation reads 'Permanently delete this resource' while the operation fetches a single virtual card and no DELETE exists for this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and remove the misleading deletion wording.

findings.title: Card creation endpoint has contradictory 201 vs 200 responses and wrong schema
findings.evidence: GET single physical card returns 201 instead of 200, POST creates physical card returns 200 with a PhysicalCard schema, and POST /cards/vault returns 201 with PCILimit schema; success codes are inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 200 for reads and 201 for creations consistently, and correct the GET /cards/physical/{card_id} success code to 200.

findings.title: Vault create operation returns limit schema, mislabelled as card creation
findings.evidence: Summary is 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' and the response is PCILimit, while the operationId is post_card_vault_creation and the path is cards/vault, so the resource returned is a limit not a card.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the operation and path to reflect the spend limit creation, or split card-detail retrieval from limit creation.

findings.title: Security-sensitive vault endpoints without documented PCI handling
findings.evidence: CardDetails returns full PAN and CVV in a 200 response, with no description of caching headers, rate limits, or restrictions; the only protection is an OAuth scope cards:read_vault.
findings.suggested_fix: Document no-store caching requirements, audit logging, and the sensitivity of the response in the operation description.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security yet 401 response
findings.evidence: The operation sets security: [] (no auth) yet documents a 401 Unauthorized response, which is contradictory for a create operation that mutates financial data.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the oauth2 reimbursements:write scope to this operation and remove the empty security override.

findings.title: Pagination inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards list uses start and page_size, with no page_size bounds in the physical cards list, and physical cards has no pagination parameters at all while returning a paginated response schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters with consistent bounds to the physical cards list and use the same pattern across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter naming style
findings.evidence: Parameter userId is camelCase while all others are snake_case like user_id; orderByAmountAsc is camelCase while order_by_amount_desc is snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId to user_id and orderByAmountAsc to order_by_amount_asc, keeping the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Ambiguous and overlapping sync filter parameters on reimbursements
findings.evidence: sync_status says it supersedes has_no_sync_commits and sync_ready, but all three remain as independent filters with no precedence stated for combinations or deprecation notice.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits as deprecated and document the precedence explicitly.

findings.title: Transaction state default is undocumented for list endpoint
findings.evidence: Description says if state is not set all transactions except declined are returned, but the state enum has no default and 'ALL' is described as special, making the default behaviour easy to misread.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the default explicitly in the schema and clarify how 'ALL' differs from the unset default.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload uses undocumented idempotency mechanisms
findings.evidence: Body has an idempotency_key field and the vault endpoint has an X-Idempotency-Key header, but the receipt upload does not use the header and the vault create operation marks the header optional, so retries have no uniform contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism across write endpoints and make it required or clearly documented as to behaviour on duplicates.

findings.title: Path naming inconsistent between reimbursement endpoints
findings.evidence: The receipt endpoint uses singular 'reimbursement' while all other reimbursement paths use plural 'reimbursements'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the path to /developer/v1/reimbursements/submit-receipt or similar plural form.

findings.title: Deprecated amount fields still returned with type conflicts
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type number while SingleTransaction.amount is type string for the same deprecated field, so the same resource returns different types depending on endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the amount type consistent across Transaction and SingleTransaction schemas.

findings.title: Card holder and reimbursement ID fields missing relationship to parent operations
findings.evidence: PhysicalCard.required includes display_name, expiration, fulfillment and last_four, which are readOnly, while id and state are not required, making the required list inconsistent with the documented response shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the required array with fields that the server always returns, and remove readOnly fields from the required list where appropriate.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH is a destructive split but not marked idempotent or documented
findings.evidence: Operation is marked "x-destructive":true and replaces existing splits, but has no idempotency guidance and no X-Idempotency-Key header, unlike POST /developer/v1/cards/vault.
findings.suggested_fix: Document replace semantics explicitly and offer an idempotency key or a conditional/version check for retries.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload defines idempotency_key in body, not header
findings.evidence: idempotency_key is a required multipart field, while POST /developer/v1/cards/vault uses an X-Idempotency-Key header (optional), and no other POST documents idempotency at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header X-Idempotency-Key) across all mutating endpoints and state whether it is required.

findings.title: Card vault POST has an optional idempotency key despite creating funds limits and cards
findings.evidence: The header is "required": false, yet the operation creates a card and a spend limit; a retry without the key may create duplicates.
findings.suggested_fix: Make X-Idempotency-Key required for this create operation or document the duplicate behavior when omitted.

findings.title: Physical card POST and vault endpoints lack documented 4xx/409 errors
findings.evidence: The 400 response is typed as a plain string schema, while every other error uses DeveloperApiErrorResponse; no 401/403/404/409 is declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Return DeveloperApiErrorResponse for 400 and declare 401, 403, 404, and 409 where applicable.

findings.title: Success status codes inconsistent for GET physical card
findings.evidence: Success is documented as 201 Created for a read operation, while the list and other GETs use 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: summary: "Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation that fetches a single virtual card; there is no DELETE on this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card'.

findings.title: Physical card DELETE described as termination; suspension verbs swapped
findings.evidence: POST is 'Suspend a card' and DELETE is 'Unsuspend a card' (correct), but the POST description says 'The suspension is revertable' with no link to the unsuspend operation; DELETE /cards/physical/{card_id} is 'Terminate a card' with the warning only in description, which conflicts with DELETE semantics for a reversible-looking resource.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the terminate operation with a non-DELETE-implying summary or document that DELETE is irreversible in the summary itself and link the suspension operations.

findings.title: Transactions 'state' filter default behavior is ambiguous
findings.evidence: Description says non-declined transactions are returned when state is unset, and the enum lacks a default, while 'ALL' is documented as including DECLINED.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit default to the schema and an example showing the default filtering.

findings.title: Inconsistent query parameter casing and sort parameter styles
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case user_id; transactions mix orderByAmountAsc with order_by_amount_desc and order_by_date_asc.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to snake_case (user_id, order_by_amount_asc) and deprecate the old names.

findings.title: Pagination param 'start' is inconsistent with cursor semantics and sort in lists
findings.evidence: 'start' is described as 'the ID of the last entity of the previous page', but physical cards list has no pagination params at all and page_size has no documented maximum in schema, only in description.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an opaque cursor named consistently (e.g. cursor) across list endpoints and add maximum/minimum to the page_size schema.

findings.title: Physical card list has pagination response but no pagination parameters
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a page.next link, yet the parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only; no start or page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters matching the other list endpoints.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no auth yet is a write
findings.evidence: "security": [] overrides global access and no scope is required, yet the endpoint creates a reimbursement; only a 401 is documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Require oauth2 with reimbursements:write scope and remove the empty security override.

findings.title: Card vault create response and tag/scope misuse for sensitive data
findings.evidence: Operation returns PCILimit containing full card PAN and CVV, and the summary says 'Create a spend limit' while the scope is 'cards:read_vault' plus 'limits:write'; the create operation is not marked with any sensitive-data flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Split spend-limit creation from sensitive detail retrieval and mark sensitive responses with a clear warning and cache-control guidance.

findings.title: Physical card fetch returns full card number in shipping
findings.evidence: CardShipping includes a 'full_card_number' string property, yet PhysicalCard returns fulfillment.shipping on GET and list endpoints marked x-uses-read-replica, with no sensitivity or scope note.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove full_card_number from non-vault responses or document it as sensitive with a distinct read_vault scope.

findings.title: Transaction 'amount' documented as deprecated but typed inconsistently
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type number while SingleTransaction.amount is type string, both marked deprecated 'Use entity_amount'; entity_amount itself uses minor-unit integers.
findings.suggested_fix: Make both schemas identical in type and state the deprecation removal date.
